svg.title: UHF RFID band map — South Africa's dual-band allocation versus the US and EU bands
svg.desc: A frequency map of the UHF RFID bands. The United States uses 902-928 MHz under FCC Part 15 and the European Union uses 865-868 MHz under ETSI EN 302 208. South Africa is a dual-band RAIN market authorised by ICASA: 865.6-867.6 MHz at 2 W ERP (the EU-harmonised sub-band), 915.4-919 MHz at 4 W EIRP with frequency hopping, and 919.2-921 MHz at 4 W EIRP for non-modulating devices. South Africa's 915.4-919 MHz band sits inside the upper part of the US 902-928 MHz band, just below Australia's 920-926 MHz band, and does not overlap the EU 865-868 MHz band. Because both bands are legal, inlays must be tuned to match the reader estate; access-control cards at 13.56 MHz are global and unaffected.
svg.text: GET THE BAND RIGHT — SOUTH AFRICA IS DUAL-BAND
ICASA permits 865.6-867.6 MHz (2 W ERP) and the higher-power 915.4-919 MHz (4 W EIRP, FHSS)
915.4-919 MHz · 4 W EIRP · FHSS | 919.2-921 MHz · 4 W EIRP · non-modulating
Plus 865.6-867.6 MHz · 2 W ERP (EU-harmonised). All ICASA-allocated — tune the inlay to your reader.
South Africa is a dual-band RAIN market
915.4-919 MHz (4 W EIRP) sits inside the upper US 902-928 MHz band, just below Australia's 920-926 MHz; 865.6-867.6 MHz mirrors the EU band.
Match the inlay to your ICASA type-approved readers. Access cards at 13.56 MHz (HF) are global and unaffected.
